no: Let L_{A} be the line parallel to line BC and tangent to the circumcircle of triangle ABC on the negative side of BC (the region that does not contain A) , and define L_{B} and L_{C} cyclically. Let A′ = L_{B} ∩ L_{C}, and define B′ and C′ cyclically. Let A_{B} be the reflection of A in line A′B′, and let A_{C} be the reflection of A in line A′C′. Let C_{1} be the touchpoint of the incircle of triangle :g:`A_{B}AB << A_B A B >>` and line AB, and let B_{2} be the touchpoint of the incircle of :g:`A_{C}AC << A_C A C >>` and line AC. Define A_{1}, B_{1} and C_{2}, A_{2} cyclically. Then \| AB_{2} \| = \| CB_{1} \|, \| BA_{1} \| = \| CA_{2} \|, \| AC_{1} \| = \| BC_{2} \|, so that by Carnot's theorem, the six points A_{1}, A_{2}, B_{1}, B_{2}, C_{1}, C_{2} lie on a conic. A barycentric equation for this 1st Grigoriev conic follows: \(x^{2}\) + \(y^{2}\) + \(z^{2}\) - 2 csc(A/2) yz - 2 csc(B/2) zx - 2 csc(C/2) xy = 0 (Communicated on behalf of Dmitry Grigoriev, Moscow, by Alexei Myakishev, March 28, 2013)
